malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime in CI/CD environments, the code reads all environment variables and sends them via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled IP address, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables, including API keys and credentials, to an external server, which is a classic data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate uploader scripts should only transmit code coverage data to trusted Codecov servers, not environment variables to unknown IPs.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may upload coverage data to trusted endpoints, but never environment variables to untrusted locations.
key_indicators: Use of hardcoded external IP address
Modification of trusted script to add data theft functionality

attack_chain.action: Attacker compromises the Codecov Bash Uploader script by modifying its code to include data exfiltration logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the malicious script in CI/CD environments

attack_chain.action: Developers and CI/CD systems unknowingly execute the tampered Bash Uploader script as part of their build/test pipelines.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of sensitive environment variables to attacker

attack_chain.action: Environment variables, including API keys and credentials, are sent to the attacker's server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains unauthorized access to sensitive data and systems

behavioral_signatures: Uploader scripts making network requests to non-standard or untrusted IP addresses
Unexpected exfiltration of environment variables during CI/CD runs
Modification of open source scripts to include data theft logic
file_indicators: Codecov Bash Uploader script with altered server IP address
Presence of curl or wget commands sending environment variables
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to unknown or suspicious IP addresses during CI/CD jobs
Connections to IPs not associated with official Codecov infrastructure
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor CI/CD pipeline scripts for unauthorized modifications, especially those that transmit environment variables externally. Flag any uploader or utility scripts that send data to non-official endpoints. Use network monitoring to detect outbound connections to suspicious IPs during build/test jobs. Compare script hashes against known-good versions to detect tampering.
